economy.summary: His campaign platform says he will cut federal regulations and unshackle job creators to get the people of southwestern Pennsylvania working again, tying job growth to reducing government red tape.
economy.short: Supports cutting regulations to expand southwestern Pennsylvania jobs.

taxes.summary: Voted for the One Big Beautiful Bill Act (H.R. 1) in July 2025, describing it as the largest tax relief package and a reduction in government spending. His campaign site says he will fight to make the 2017 tax cuts permanent.
taxes.short: Supports permanent 2017 tax cuts; voted for 2025 tax bill.

abortion.summary: Co-sponsored the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act and the Pain-Capable Unborn Children from Late-Term Abortions Act, and has voted against federal funding of abortion, per the Susan B. Anthony Pro-Life America national scorecard.
abortion.short: Co-sponsored abortion restriction bills; opposes federal abortion funding.

education.summary: Co-sponsored the Parents Bill of Rights Act (H.R. 5), which would require schools to disclose curricula and give parents a right to be heard, saying parents play a critical role in their child's education.
education.short: Co-sponsored Parents Bill of Rights requiring school curriculum disclosure.

healthcare.summary: His official issues page supports access to affordable coverage through free-market solutions rather than government mandates, ensuring coverage for pre-existing conditions, and reforms to lower prescription drug costs.
healthcare.short: Supports market-based coverage, pre-existing-condition protections, lower drug costs.

energy.summary: Supports expanding Pennsylvania natural gas and coal production, citing jobs and energy prices; supported H.R. 1121 to block a presidential moratorium on hydraulic fracturing and legislation to repeal a proposed natural gas tax.
energy.short: Supports natural gas and coal production; opposes fracking moratorium.

guns.summary: Co-sponsored H.R. 38, the Constitutional Concealed Carry Reciprocity Act of 2025, which would require states to recognize concealed-carry permits issued by other states.
guns.short: Co-sponsored national concealed-carry permit reciprocity bill.

economy.summary: His campaign platform calls for policies that raise wages, strengthen workers' rights, and expand opportunities for small businesses, along with investing in job training, modern infrastructure, and education.
economy.short: Proposes raising wages, workers' rights, small-business and job-training investment.

taxes.summary: Proposes reforming the tax code to reward work over wealth as part of his economic security platform; he has also criticized the 2025 tax law, saying its biggest benefits accrue to those who already earn the most.
taxes.short: Proposes tax code reform rewarding work over wealth.

education.summary: His economic security platform includes investing in education alongside job training and infrastructure as a way to expand opportunity in the district.
education.short: Proposes investing in education, job training, and infrastructure.

healthcare.summary: Supports a universal healthcare system that would cover every American and lower out-of-pocket costs, saying healthcare should be guaranteed as a right, not a privilege; also calls for ending medical debt and has raised concerns about Medicaid cuts affecting rural hospitals.
healthcare.short: Supports universal healthcare covering everyone; opposes Medicaid cuts.

guns.summary: Says he supports enhanced and universal background checks but would not support a ban on assault rifles, saying candidates have to meet voters where they are in a gun-centered culture.
guns.short: Supports universal background checks; opposes assault-rifle ban.
